purpose: separate finite-batch cutoff-tie behavior from the no-ties QB derivation and test candidate coordinate-minimizer representatives without granting model or training authority

finite_batch_problem.source_assumption: Eq. 14's exact-load statement assumes no ties at the selected expert threshold
finite_batch_problem.structural_tie: when expert j is token i's biased top-(k+1) cutoff, r_ij = alpha_i - s_ij equals current bias b_j exactly; repeated cutoff identity therefore creates repeated required-bias values even for continuous random raw scores
finite_batch_problem.valid_rank_bracket: for target q and threshold tau, count(r < tau) <= q < count(r <= tau)
finite_batch_problem.actual_topk_dependency: equal biased scores are resolved by a top-k implementation's tie behavior, so rank-bracket validity alone does not guarantee realized exact loads
finite_batch_problem.gauge: mean-centering all next biases preserves next-step top-k selection but changes their absolute position relative to discarded old cutoffs

observed_discovery.score_distribution: torch.float64 Uniform[0,1), with mean-centered Normal(0,0.15) initial expert bias
observed_discovery.cycle_identity: all mean-centered bias coordinates rounded to 14 decimal places
observed_discovery.interpretation: bin interpolation and interval-midpoint selection can break endpoint equalities on fixed scores, but this discovery set cannot select a local policy or predict changing-score training
